newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian Breweries opens public share offer.
newsitem.headline: Zambian Breweries opens public share offer.

text.p: Zambian Breweries opened its offer of 13 million ordinary shares on Monday ahead of its planned listing on the Lusaka Stock Exchange on June 6.

"The Zambia Privatisation Trust Fund (ZPTF) is offering 13 million shares, representing 10 percent of Zambian Breweries issued share capital, for sale at a price of 150 kwacha (12 U.S. cents) per share," a company official said.
"The offer is open to all Zambian citizens and eligible institutions and is intended to result in a broad distribution of Zambian Breweries shares among Zambian citizens," the official added.
The offer closes on May 9 ahead of the proposed listing.

Zambian Breweries is co-owned by Zamanglo Industrial Corp Ltd (ZAMIC), a subsidiary of Anglo American Corp of South Africa, which has an effective 15 percent interest in South African Breweries Ltd (SAB).
Ten percent of the issued share capital, representing 13 million shares, was transferred for consideration to the Zambia Privatisation Trust Fund (ZPTF) to be held in trust for sale to the public.
A portion of the 13 million shares, not exceeding 1.3 million shares, will be offered preferentially, but at the same price per share, to Zambia employees of Zambian Breweries.

Zambian Breweries has undergone extensive rehabilitation over the past 30 months, raising machine efficiency from 56 percent at the end of the 1993 financial year to around 65 percent capacity utilisation.
The company forecasts a gross turnover of 58 billion kwacha in 1997 from 47 billion kwacha in 1996 with retained profits rising to around 1.05 billion kwacha from 0.85 billion kwacha.

Zambian Breweries listing will bring to seven the number of companies listed on the Lusaka Stock Exchange after Chilanga Cement, Farmers House, Rothmans, Zambia Sugar, Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines and Trans Zambezi Industries.
